verdict.rationale: Cactus documents running its platform from a coding agent with an API key, backed by an agent-readable llms.txt. Some API steps also take plain-language input, such as a product description that /tool_schemas turns into tool definitions. Beyond that, natural-language operation of the product depends on an external agent rather than a first-party conversational interface. Hands-on reports on the Needle command model are mixed: direct phrasings often work, but indirect commands frequently misfire. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language control surface for the platform itself, documented examples of agent-driven workflows, and reliable handling of indirect natural-language commands.
